title: Isolate long-tail variance and simplify load adapters in eval pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
The eval + perf regression pipeline has accumulated several ad-hoc load adapters and global state that make repeatable benchmarking difficult. Long-tail variance (spikes in 95/99th latency) is often caused by test harness flakiness rather than real runtime regressions. This ticket refactors the pipeline to: (1) introduce a stable adapter interface for load sources, (2) remove shared mutable globals from the synthetic load generators, (3) normalize metric tags and sample windows, and (4) upgrade and pin test dependencies so CI runs are deterministic across agents.

Goals / Scope:
- Create a minimal, well-documented LoadAdapter interface with clear contracts for lifecycle, sample rates, and deterministic seeding.
- Replace three bespoke adapters (legacy_http_adapter, local_kv_adapter, grpc_stitch_adapter) with the new interface via thin shims.
- Eliminate global singletons used by the synthetic runner (cache, RNG, config) and pass context objects explicitly.
- Standardize metrics emitted (service, model_variant, sequence_len_bucket, run_id) and ensure tags are consistent across local, CI, and staging runs.
- Upgrade k6 -> 0.46.0 for stable JS runtime and pin Python test deps (pytest, pyyaml) in a lockfile.
- Add deterministic seeding option for smoke/regression runs and a lightweight golden-baseline comparator for 95/99 latency deltas.

Out of scope:
- Rewriting the entire load generation system or changing scheduling architecture. Full tracing and sampling overhaul to be separate follow-up.

Acceptance criteria (must pass to close):
- New LoadAdapter interface has documentation and two reference implementations (http shim + kv shim) checked into the repo.
- No use of the previous global RNG or cache singletons in the synthetic runner; CI lint rule enforces this pattern.
- CI regression job runs deterministically for three consecutive runs (same seed) and the golden-baseline comparator flags only real regressions.
- k6 and Python deps upgraded and lockfile committed; a CI job verifies dependency checksum.
- Metric normalization implemented and validated against staging dashboards (match expected tag set).

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Interface design focuses on minimal surface area: start()/stop(), next_request(), and teardown(context). This keeps adapters simple and migratable.
- We prefer thin shims over immediate rewrite to reduce landing risk; each shim maps legacy config keys into the new typed config.
- Deterministic seeding improves reproducibility but may hide concurrency-related nondeterminism; tests using deterministic seeds should be complemented by periodic randomized stress runs.

Migration plan (phased):
1) Spike (2 days): prototype LoadAdapter API in a sandbox package, implement http shim.
2) Refactor core runner (4 days): remove globals, thread explicit context through handlers, add lint checks.
3) Adapter migration (6 days): implement shims for the remaining adapters and switch CI to use new adapters behind a feature flag.
4) Dependency work (2 days): upgrade k6 and pin Python deps, add CI checksum step.
5) Validation & rollout (4 days): run 10 deterministic CI runs, compare to golden baseline, enable for all regression jobs.

Testing & CI requirements:
- Unit tests for LoadAdapter contract (mocked RNG/context).
- Integration test in staging that runs a low-load smoke scenario and validates tag parity.
- CI gating: disallow merges to main unless dependency checksum job and adapter-unit tests pass.

Links / references:
- Design note: https://confluence.internal.redwood/eng/eval-refactor (placeholder)
- Related tickets: ENG-30501 (driver decomposition) and ENG-37299 (perf sandbox modernization)
- Example golden baseline outputs: gs://redwood-evals/baselines/2025-07-01.json

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Shims leaking legacy behavior -> mitigation: strict unit tests + code review checklist.
- Risk: Deterministic runs masking real flakiness -> mitigation: keep periodic randomized CI stress and document in README.
- Risk: Dependency upgrade causing runtime incompatibility -> mitigation: run canary k6 job on staging before enabling for regression CI.
